summary: This August 2021 post theorizes that Citadel's failures to deliver GME shares placed Robinhood under a 35-day SHO Rule obligation that triggered the January 28 trading halt. The author speculates that Citadel engineered this arrangement to force other market participants into delivery obligations, effectively holding them "hostage" and preventing Citadel's own squeeze. The post argues regulators have been secretly negotiating a solution and that the MOASS is delayed pending new regulations. The author labels their analysis conspiratorial and speculative throughout.

key_claims.claim: Robinhood halted trading on January 28, 2021, precisely on day 35 of GME's 39-day run on the SEC threshold securities list, because Robinhood became legally liable to deliver shares after 35 days under SHO Rule 242.203(b2)
key_claims.note: SHO Rule threshold exists and is correctly described; the specific timing claim (day 35 of 39) cannot be independently verified from the text sample, and SEC findings attributed the halt to capital/liquidity pressures rather than delivery obligations.

key_claims.claim: Citadel intentionally created delivery failures to force Robinhood and other brokers into the position of being squeezed before Citadel itself
key_claims.note: No evidence in any SEC filing, regulator investigation, or court case substantiates coordinated manipulation by Citadel. SEC October 2021 report found positive-sentiment buying, not orchestrated short-covering mechanics, drove the spike.

key_claims.claim: A MOASS (Mother of All Short Squeezes) will eventually occur once regulators safely unwind the delivery and rehypothecation problems Citadel created
key_claims.note: By 2026, no MOASS materialized. GME peaked at ~$483 intraday Jan 28, 2021; subsequent peaks (~$65 May-June 2024) fell far short of predictions of thousands or millions per share.

key_claims.claim: The cost basis errors Robinhood customers saw when transferring shares to other brokers occurred because Robinhood had to repurchase shares at market prices after Citadel failed to deliver them
key_claims.note: Plausible explanation but unverified. Alternative causes for cost basis discrepancies exist, and the text provides no documentary evidence linking these to failed deliveries.

key_claims.claim: Market activity in February 2021 represented whales fighting to prevent Citadel from escaping its trap and forcing the broader system into chaos
key_claims.note: Purely speculative interpretation of normal market volatility. No documented evidence of coordinated whale activity with this motive.

key_claims.claim: Citadel and involved regulators will receive minimal punishment because they negotiated a secret deal to manage the orderly unwinding of the crisis
key_claims.note: No major regulatory action against Citadel materialized by 2026, but not for the theorized reason (no substantiated hostage arrangement existed to require negotiation).

validity_rationale: Core predictions (MOASS) failed to materialize. Central explanations for the Robinhood halt contradict SEC October 2021 findings, which attributed the halt to capital/liquidity requirements and cited positive-sentiment buying as the primary driver, not orchestrated delivery manipulation. The 'hostage' conspiracy theory lacks any substantiation from regulators, markets, or documented investigations. While SHO Rule mechanics are described accurately, they are misapplied to construct an unfounded conspiracy narrative.
